text:
Jack Drury plays the minutes nobody notices for a Nashville team that has won seven straight: 17.18 a night, up more than a minute over his last ten games, with 25 blocked shots. The Denver Post covered his Nov 5 return to Ball Arena with Ross Colton, two former Avalanche forwards now settled in Nashville.

The scoring is thin: 5 points in 20 games, and his own chances (0.48 expected goals per 60, a measure of chance quality) sit below last season's 0.67 in Colorado. His points rate is under the bottom of our talent range, and he ranks 500th of 528 skaters in our wins added. That measure is built from goals, though, and Drury's value shows up elsewhere. Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting 0.26 fewer expected goals per 60 with him on the ice last season, 99th percentile among forwards, with the caveat that his Colorado teammates were strong (98th percentile). This season the Predators' share of five-on-five expected goals is slightly better with him on than off. Friday in Vegas he put four shots on goal, his most in ten games. If you're watching him for points, you're watching the wrong thing.
headline: Jack Drury's case is made in his own end
